_meta: The royal inscription programme standing in 467 BCE on the Persepolis Terrace and at Naqsh-e Rustam, copy by copy, and what the build carves of it (Phase 8 review A-M5; D-177; research/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md Q-290). Locations: research/LANGUAGES.md §2 (the published find-spots and locations, via the Livius page descriptions read through the scrape; facts only) and the SITE_SPEC rows named. `carved`: the number of copies of each version the build carves (tests/inscriptions.test.ts counts them in the built world); `missing`: copies or versions standing in 467 that are NOT carved, each with why; `hidden`: texts that existed in 467 but were not visible (sealed or buried), correctly not on any surface. Every missing row is a placeholder (flagged in the dev overlay through the inscriptions group and the world summary line). Texts of Artaxerxes I and later (A1P, A2, A3Pa) postdate 467 and are absent by chronology. Small inscribed objects (door knobs DPi, XPi; weights, vessels) belong to the props workstream and are listed only for completeness.
